spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m3p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Copies == {"c1", "c2"}
Nodes  == {"n1", "n2", "n3"}
Patrons == {"p1", "p2"}
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES leader, term, alive, alloc, inbox

vars == <<leader, term, alive, alloc, inbox>>

\* alloc[c] records the patron holding copy c together with the term of the
\* leader that granted it (NONE means the copy is still free).
FreeRec == [patron |-> NONE, term |-> 0]

LiveLeader == (leader # NONE) /\ alive[leader]

Init ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ term = 0
    /\ alive = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]
    /\ alloc = [c \in Copies |-> FreeRec]
    /\ inbox = {}

\* A live node with no current live leader wins a fresh, higher-numbered term.
Elect(n) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ ~ LiveLeader
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, alloc, inbox>>

\* The leader may crash silently; its in-flight grant messages remain queued.
Crash ==
    /\ LiveLeader
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![leader] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, alloc, inbox>>

\* The current leader posts a grant of a free copy to a patron; the message
\* carries the leader's term and rides an unordered fabric.
Grant(c, p) ==
    /\ LiveLeader
    /\ alloc[c].patron = NONE
    /\ ~ \E m \in inbox : m.copy = c
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[copy |-> c, patron |-> p, term |-> term]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, alive, alloc>>

\* Grants are delivered in any order. A grant commits only if the copy is still
\* free and the grant is not stale (its term is at least the copy's last term).
Deliver(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ alloc[m.copy].patron = NONE
    /\ m.term >= alloc[m.copy].term
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![m.copy] = [patron |-> m.patron, term |-> m.term]]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, alive>>

\* A stale grant (from a term no longer relevant) is simply dropped.
DropStale(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ alloc[m.copy].patron # NONE
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, alive, alloc>>

\* When every node has crashed the system idles (stutters) rather than deadlock.
AllDead == \A n \in Nodes : ~ alive[n]

Idle ==
    /\ AllDead
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ Idle
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ Crash
    \/ \E c \in Copies, p \in Patrons : Grant(c, p)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Deliver(m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : DropStale(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {NONE}
    /\ term \in Nat
    /\ alive \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ alloc \in [Copies -> [patron : Patrons \cup {NONE}, term : Nat]]
    /\ inbox \subseteq [copy : Copies, patron : Patrons, term : Nat]

\* No copy is ever handed to a second patron: once a copy is held, every grant
\* message still in flight for that copy names the very patron already holding it.
NoDoubleAlloc ==
    \A c \in Copies :
        alloc[c].patron # NONE =>
            \A m \in inbox : (m.copy = c) => (m.patron = alloc[c].patron)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAlloc
nl:
A library runs a book-reservation service across three server nodes that share a
small pool of physical copies of a title. Exactly one node acts as leader and is
the only node allowed to grant a copy to a waiting patron. Nodes run a simple
leader election: when there is no live leader, any live node can win a fresh,
strictly higher-numbered term and become leader. The leader can crash silently
at any time, after which the surviving nodes elect a new leader on a higher term.
When the leader grants a free copy to a patron it posts a grant message stamped
with its term onto an unordered message fabric, so grant messages may be
delivered to the allocation store in any order. A delivered grant commits only
if the copy is still free and the grant is not stale relative to the copy's last
recorded term; a grant found to be stale (its copy already held) is dropped
rather than applied.
If every node has crashed the service simply idles until a node returns.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A copy that is already held by a patron is never reassigned to a different patron, even across leader failover and reordered grant messages.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m7p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Sorters == {"s1", "s2"}
Bags    == {"b1", "b2"}
Chutes  == {"h1", "h2"}
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES reg, pending, crashed, routed

vars == <<reg, pending, crashed, routed>>

\* reg[c] is the compare-and-swap register for chute c (the bag it currently
\* holds, or NONE). routed logs every (bag, chute) pair a CAS ever committed.
Init ==
    /\ reg = [c \in Chutes |-> NONE]
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ routed = {}

BagRouted(b) == \E p \in routed : p.bag = b
BagPending(b) == \E r \in pending : r.bag = b

\* A live sorter snapshots a chute register and proposes routing a not-yet-routed
\* bag there via compare-and-swap (expected value = the snapshot it just read).
Submit(s, b, c) ==
    /\ s \notin crashed
    /\ ~ BagRouted(b)
    /\ ~ BagPending(b)
    /\ reg[c] = NONE
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {[bag |-> b, chute |-> c, exp |-> reg[c], sorter |-> s]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, crashed, routed>>

\* CAS succeeds: the register still equals the expected snapshot, so it is
\* swapped to the bag and the routing is committed to the log.
Apply(r) ==
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ reg[r.chute] = r.exp
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![r.chute] = r.bag]
    /\ routed' = routed \cup {[bag |-> r.bag, chute |-> r.chute]}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* CAS fails: the register moved since the snapshot, so the attempt is discarded
\* and the bag is free to be resubmitted (retry) elsewhere.
Reject(r) ==
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ reg[r.chute] # r.exp
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, crashed, routed>>

\* A sorter can crash silently; its already-queued requests remain and are
\* resolved by Apply/Reject like any other.
Crash(s) ==
    /\ s \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, pending, routed>>

Quiescent ==
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ (\A b \in Bags : BagRouted(b)) \/ (crashed = Sorters)

Idle ==
    /\ Quiescent
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Sorters, b \in Bags, c \in Chutes : Submit(s, b, c)
    \/ \E r \in pending : Apply(r)
    \/ \E r \in pending : Reject(r)
    \/ \E s \in Sorters : Crash(s)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [Chutes -> Bags \cup {NONE}]
    /\ pending \subseteq [bag : Bags, chute : Chutes, exp : Bags \cup {NONE}, sorter : Sorters]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Sorters
    /\ routed \subseteq [bag : Bags, chute : Chutes]

\* Every committed routing still matches what its chute's register holds: no chute
\* is ever swapped out from under an earlier committed bag, so a slot is never
\* allocated to two bags.
NoDoubleAlloc ==
    \A p \in routed : reg[p.chute] = p.bag
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAlloc
nl:
An airport baggage router sends each bag to exactly one outbound chute. Each
chute has a hardware compare-and-swap register that names the bag currently
assigned to it (or reads free). Sorting units race to claim free chutes: a live
sorter reads a chute's register, and if it reads free it submits a
compare-and-swap request to place a bag there, carrying the free value it just
observed as the expected value. When the request is applied the swap succeeds
only if the register still equals that expected value; otherwise the register
moved (another sorter won the chute first) and the request is rejected, leaving
the bag free to be resubmitted to another chute. A sorter may crash silently at
any point; requests it already queued are still resolved normally by later apply
or reject steps. When all bags are placed, or every sorter has crashed, the
router idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Once a bag has been committed to a chute, that chute's register never changes to a different bag, so no chute is ever allocated to two bags.

---- MODULE W4Od14m3p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Drones == {"d1", "d2", "d3"}
MsgIds == {1, 2, 3}
TOTAL == 4
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES leader, term, alive, held, transit

vars == <<leader, term, alive, held, transit>>

\* Sum of a function's values over a finite domain.
RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN f[x] + SumOver(f, S \ {x})

RECURSIVE SumTransit(_)
SumTransit(T) ==
    IF T = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET m == CHOOSE y \in T : TRUE
         IN m.amt + SumTransit(T \ {m})

LiveLeader == (leader # NONE) /\ alive[leader]

Init ==
    /\ leader = "d1"
    /\ term = 1
    /\ alive = [d \in Drones |-> TRUE]
    /\ held = [d \in Drones |-> IF d = "d1" THEN TOTAL ELSE 0]
    /\ transit = {}

\* When there is no live leader a surviving drone wins a higher term and leads.
Elect(d) ==
    /\ alive[d]
    /\ ~ LiveLeader
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, held, transit>>

\* The leader may crash silently; the surveillance tokens it still holds stay put
\* (counted, never destroyed) and the swarm elects a new leader.
Crash ==
    /\ LiveLeader
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![leader] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, held, transit>>

\* The leader hands one surveillance token it holds to another drone by posting a
\* transfer message on an unordered link (an unused message id).
Send(dst, id) ==
    /\ LiveLeader
    /\ dst # leader
    /\ held[leader] >= 1
    /\ ~ \E m \in transit : m.id = id
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![leader] = @ - 1]
    /\ transit' = transit \cup {[id |-> id, to |-> dst, amt |-> 1]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, alive>>

\* Transfer messages arrive in any order; delivery credits the recipient.
Deliver(m) ==
    /\ m \in transit
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![m.to] = @ + m.amt]
    /\ transit' = transit \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, alive>>

AllDead == \A d \in Drones : ~ alive[d]

Idle ==
    /\ AllDead
    /\ transit = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Elect(d)
    \/ Crash
    \/ \E dst \in Drones, id \in MsgIds : Send(dst, id)
    \/ \E m \in transit : Deliver(m)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Drones \cup {NONE}
    /\ term \in Nat
    /\ alive \in [Drones -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ held \in [Drones -> 0..TOTAL]
    /\ transit \subseteq [id : MsgIds, to : Drones, amt : {1}]

\* No surveillance token is ever created or destroyed: the count held across all
\* drones plus the count riding the links is always exactly the swarm total.
Conservation ==
    SumOver(held, Drones) + SumTransit(transit) = TOTAL
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm shares a fixed budget of surveillance
tokens, each token representing one sector of airspace that must stay covered.
One drone acts as the coordinating leader and is the only drone allowed to
rebalance coverage. When there is no live leader, any surviving drone wins a
strictly higher term and takes over as leader (failover). The leader can crash
silently at any time; the tokens it was still holding remain parked on that
drone (they are never lost) while the swarm elects a new leader on a higher term.
To rebalance, the leader hands one token it holds to another drone by posting a
transfer message onto an unordered radio link, tagged with an unused message id;
because the link is unordered, transfer messages may be delivered in any order,
and delivery simply credits the recipient drone with the token. When every drone
has crashed and no transfer is in flight, the swarm idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of surveillance tokens held across all drones plus those in flight on the links is always exactly the swarm's fixed total, so no token is ever created or destroyed.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m2p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Surgeries == {"x1", "x2", "x3"}
Parts == {"surgeon", "anesth", "room"}
CAP == 2
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES phase, prop, votes, inbox, used

vars == <<phase, prop, votes, inbox, used>>

Votes == {"yes", "no"}
Phases == {"idle", "voting", "committed", "aborted"}

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ prop = NONE
    /\ votes = [p \in Parts |-> NONE]
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ used = 0

\* The coordinator opens a two-phase-commit round to book an as-yet-unbooked
\* surgery into a free operating-room block.
Propose(x) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ prop' = x
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ votes' = [p \in Parts |-> NONE]
    /\ inbox' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED used

\* Each participant posts a yes/no vote onto an unordered fabric.
CastVote(p, v) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[p] = NONE
    /\ ~ \E m \in inbox : m.part = p
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[part |-> p, v |-> v]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, prop, votes, used>>

\* Votes are delivered to the coordinator in any order.
Deliver(m) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ votes[m.part] = NONE
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![m.part] = m.v]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, prop, used>>

\* Commit requires unanimous yes AND a free room block; it consumes one unit of
\* room capacity.
Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A p \in Parts : votes[p] = "yes"
    /\ used < CAP
    /\ used' = used + 1
    /\ phase' = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prop, votes, inbox>>

\* Any no vote, or no free block, aborts the round.
Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ (\E p \in Parts : votes[p] = "no") \/ (\A p \in Parts : votes[p] = "yes" /\ used >= CAP)
    /\ phase' = "aborted"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prop, votes, inbox, used>>

Reset ==
    /\ phase \in {"committed", "aborted"}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ prop' = NONE
    /\ votes' = [p \in Parts |-> NONE]
    /\ inbox' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED used

Next ==
    \/ \E x \in Surgeries : Propose(x)
    \/ \E p \in Parts, v \in Votes : CastVote(p, v)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Deliver(m)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in Phases
    /\ prop \in Surgeries \cup {NONE}
    /\ votes \in [Parts -> Votes \cup {NONE}]
    /\ inbox \subseteq [part : Parts, v : Votes]
    /\ used \in 0..CAP

\* The number of committed operating-room bookings never exceeds room capacity.
BoundedCapacity == used <= CAP
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler books surgeries into a limited number of
concurrent operating-room blocks. Because a booking must reserve the surgeon,
the anesthesia team, and the room all at once, the scheduler uses two-phase
commit: a coordinator opens a round to book one surgery, and each of the three
participants returns a yes or no vote. Votes travel over an unordered hospital
message bus, so they accumulate and may be delivered to the coordinator in any
order. The coordinator commits the booking only when all three participants
voted yes and a room block is still free, consuming one unit of capacity; if any
participant voted no, or no block remains free, the round aborts. After a commit
or abort the coordinator resets to idle and can open a new round.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of committed operating-room bookings never exceeds the fixed room-block capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od18m0p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Controllers == {"c1", "c2", "c3"}
MAXV == 6
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES owner, version, pc, snap

vars == <<owner, version, pc, snap>>

\* pc[c]: "idle" (not interested), "want" (has read a version snapshot and is
\* trying to grab the lock), "crit" (holds the door lock).
Init ==
    /\ owner = NONE
    /\ version = 0
    /\ pc = [c \in Controllers |-> "idle"]
    /\ snap = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]

\* Optimistic read: a controller records the current lock version and intends to
\* acquire.
Read(c) ==
    /\ pc[c] = "idle"
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![c] = "want"]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, version>>

\* Acquire succeeds only if the lock is free AND the version is unchanged since
\* the read (nobody bumped it in between); acquiring bumps the version.
Acquire(c) ==
    /\ pc[c] = "want"
    /\ owner = NONE
    /\ version = snap[c]
    /\ version < MAXV
    /\ owner' = c
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![c] = "crit"]
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

\* Optimistic retry: if the lock is taken or the version moved, the attempt is
\* abandoned and the controller returns to idle to re-read later.
Retry(c) ==
    /\ pc[c] = "want"
    /\ (owner # NONE) \/ (version # snap[c])
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, version, snap>>

\* A controller can be slow: while wanting the lock it may simply not act yet.
\* It never fails, so it stays eligible to acquire or retry.
Slow(c) ==
    /\ pc[c] = "want"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

\* Releasing the lock frees it and bumps the version.
Release(c) ==
    /\ pc[c] = "crit"
    /\ owner = c
    /\ owner' = NONE
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Read(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Acquire(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Retry(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Slow(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Release(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in Controllers \cup {NONE}
    /\ version \in 0..MAXV
    /\ pc \in [Controllers -> {"idle", "want", "crit"}]
    /\ snap \in [Controllers -> 0..MAXV]

\* Mutual exclusion: anyone inside the critical section is the recorded lock
\* owner. Since the lock has a single owner, at most one controller is ever
\* inside at a time.
MutualExclusion == \A c \in Controllers : (pc[c] = "crit") => (owner = c)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network lets several controllers contend for exclusive
control of a shared door lock, the critical resource. The lock exposes a version
counter and uses optimistic locking with retry: a controller first reads the
current version, then tries to acquire the lock. The acquire succeeds only if
the lock is still free and its version is unchanged since the read, meaning no
other controller slipped in; a successful acquire bumps the version and enters
the critical section. If, by acquire time, the lock is already held or the
version has moved, the controller abandons the attempt and returns to idle to
re-read and try again later. A controller may be slow, simply not acting for a
while, but it never fails, so it stays eligible to acquire or retry. Releasing
the lock frees it and bumps the version again.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At any moment at most one controller holds the door lock, because anyone in the critical section is the lock's single recorded owner.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m5p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Cars == {"e1", "e2"}
Controllers == {"q1", "q2", "q3"}
QUORUM == 2
CAP == 3
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES load, phase, votes, pend

vars == <<load, phase, votes, pend>>

Votes == {"yes", "no"}

Init ==
    /\ load = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ votes = [q \in Controllers |-> NONE]
    /\ pend = NONE

YesCount == Cardinality({q \in Controllers : votes[q] = "yes"})
AllVoted == \A q \in Controllers : votes[q] # NONE

\* Dispatch opens a quorum vote on admitting one more passenger to a car.
ProposeBoard(c) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ pend' = c
    /\ votes' = [q \in Controllers |-> NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED load

\* Each controller casts a single yes/no vote on the open proposal.
Vote(q, v) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[q] = NONE
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![q] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, phase, pend>>

\* Board succeeds only with a yes quorum AND spare capacity in the target car.
Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ YesCount >= QUORUM
    /\ load[pend] < CAP
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![pend] = @ + 1]
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ pend' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED votes

\* The proposal fails when everyone has voted but no yes quorum with capacity
\* exists.
Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ AllVoted
    /\ ~(YesCount >= QUORUM /\ load[pend] < CAP)
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ pend' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, votes>>

\* A passenger leaving a car needs no vote.
Alight(c) ==
    /\ load[c] > 0
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![c] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, pend>>

\* A privileged admin can force one boarding without a quorum, but the car's
\* capacity limit is still honored.
AdminOverride(c) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ load[c] < CAP
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, pend>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cars : ProposeBoard(c)
    \/ \E q \in Controllers, v \in Votes : Vote(q, v)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Alight(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : AdminOverride(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ load \in [Cars -> 0..CAP]
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting"}
    /\ votes \in [Controllers -> Votes \cup {NONE}]
    /\ pend \in Cars \cup {NONE}

\* No elevator car ever carries more passengers than its capacity, whether the
\* boarding was quorum-approved or forced by the admin override.
BoundedCapacity == \A c \in Cars : load[c] <= CAP
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper is governed by a set of dispatch controllers.
Admitting a passenger to a car is a safety-relevant action, so it is decided by
quorum voting: dispatch opens a proposal to board one more passenger into a
specific car, each controller casts a single yes or no vote, and the boarding
commits only if a yes quorum is reached and the target car still has spare
capacity. If everyone has voted and there is no yes quorum with capacity, the
proposal aborts. Passengers leaving a car need no vote and simply reduce its
load. A privileged building admin can override the quorum and force a single
boarding directly, but even the override honors the car's hard capacity limit.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No elevator car ever carries more passengers than its capacity, whether a boarding was quorum-approved or forced by the admin override.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m9p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Instances == {"A", "B"}
Vals == {"v1", "v2"}
MAXVER == 2
MAXE == 2
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES rec, applied, epoch, pending

vars == <<rec, applied, epoch, pending>>

\* rec is the shared runway-assignment record: a value plus a version counter.
\* applied logs (version, value) for every committed write. Each allocator
\* instance has at most one outstanding request in pending.
NoReq == [val |-> NONE, exp |-> 0, ep |-> 0]

Init ==
    /\ rec = [val |-> "init", ver |-> 0]
    /\ applied = {[ver |-> 0, val |-> "init"]}
    /\ epoch = 1
    /\ pending = [inst \in Instances |-> NoReq]

\* An allocator instance reads the record and proposes a new value, stamping its
\* request with the version it read (expected) and the current epoch.
Propose(inst, v) ==
    /\ rec.ver < MAXVER
    /\ pending[inst].val = NONE
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![inst] = [val |-> v, exp |-> rec.ver, ep |-> epoch]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, applied, epoch>>

\* A write commits only if it is from the current epoch AND its expected version
\* still matches the record (compare-and-set), which prevents a stale read from
\* clobbering an intervening write. The version advances by one.
Commit(inst) ==
    /\ pending[inst].val # NONE
    /\ pending[inst].ep = epoch
    /\ pending[inst].exp = rec.ver
    /\ rec' = [val |-> pending[inst].val, ver |-> rec.ver + 1]
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {[ver |-> rec.ver + 1, val |-> pending[inst].val]}
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![inst] = NoReq]
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

\* A request from an old epoch, or one whose expected version has been overtaken,
\* is rejected (not applied) so the losing writer must re-read and retry.
RejectStale(inst) ==
    /\ pending[inst].val # NONE
    /\ (pending[inst].ep # epoch) \/ (pending[inst].exp # rec.ver)
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![inst] = NoReq]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, applied, epoch>>

    /\ AllIdle
    /\ rec.ver = MAXVER
    /\ epoch = MAXE
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

    \/ \E inst \in Instances : Commit(inst)
    \/ \E inst \in Instances : RejectStale(inst)
    \/ Reconfig
    \/ Idle

    /\ rec \in [val : Vals \cup {"init"}, ver : 0..MAXVER]
    /\ applied \subseteq [ver : 0..MAXVER, val : Vals \cup {"init"}]
    /\ epoch \in 1..MAXE
    /\ pending \in [Instances -> [val : Vals \cup {NONE}, exp : 0..MAXVER, ep : 0..MAXE]]

\* No committed update is ever silently lost: no applied write claims a version
\* beyond the record's, and whichever applied write holds the record's current
\* version agrees with the record's current value (a clobbered write would leave
\* a stale applied entry at the top version disagreeing with the record).

        /\ (a.ver = rec.ver) => (a.val = rec.val)

An air-traffic runway allocator keeps a single shared assignment record for a
pool of runways, and two independent allocator instances update it concurrently.
The record carries a value and a version counter. To avoid lost updates, each
instance reads the record and proposes a new value stamped with the version it
read (its expected version) and the current configuration epoch. A proposed
write commits only if it belongs to the current epoch and its expected version
still matches the record, a compare-and-set that stops a stale read from
clobbering an update another instance committed in the meantime; committing
advances the version by one and logs the applied write. A write whose epoch is
old, or whose expected version has been overtaken, is rejected so its instance
must re-read and retry. Epoch-numbered reconfiguration bumps the epoch, making
any in-flight requests from the previous epoch stale. When both instances are
idle and the record and epoch have reached their bounds, the allocator idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No committed update to the shared record is ever silently overwritten, so the write holding the record's current version always agrees with the record's current value.

EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

OrderIds == {1, 2, 3}
Levels == {"L1", "L2"}
CAP == 2
MAXE == 3

VARIABLES epoch, book, inbox, admitted

vars == <<epoch, book, inbox, admitted>>

\* book[l] = number of orders currently resting at price level l (bounded by CAP).
\* inbox is the unordered set of order messages; admitted logs (id,level) pairs
\* that have been placed in the book.
Init ==
    /\ epoch = 1
    /\ book = [l \in Levels |-> 0]
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ admitted = {}

IdInFlight(i) == (\E m \in inbox : m.id = i) \/ (\E a \in admitted : a.id = i)

\* A trader submits an order for a level, stamped with the current auction epoch.
Submit(i, l) ==
    /\ ~ IdInFlight(i)
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[id |-> i, lvl |-> l, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, book, admitted>>

\* Orders are delivered in any order. An order rests in the book only if it is
\* from the current epoch AND the level still has spare capacity.
Accept(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.ep = epoch
    /\ book[m.lvl] < CAP
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![m.lvl] = @ + 1]
    /\ admitted' = admitted \cup {[id |-> m.id, lvl |-> m.lvl]}
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

    /\ m.ep # epoch
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, book, admitted>>

Cancel(a) ==
    /\ a \in admitted
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![a.lvl] = @ - 1]
    /\ admitted' = admitted \ {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inbox>>

\* Epoch-numbered reconfiguration starts a fresh auction round: the epoch bumps
\* and the book clears, so any in-flight orders from the prior round go stale.
Reconfig ==
    /\ epoch < MAXE
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ book' = [l \in Levels |-> 0]
    /\ admitted' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED inbox

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in OrderIds, l \in Levels : Submit(i, l)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Accept(m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : RejectStale(m)
    \/ \E a \in admitted : Cancel(a)
    \/ Reconfig

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 1..MAXE
    /\ book \in [Levels -> 0..CAP]
    /\ inbox \subseteq [id : OrderIds, lvl : Levels, ep : 1..MAXE]
    /\ admitted \subseteq [id : OrderIds, lvl : Levels]

\* No price level ever holds more resting orders than its capacity, across epoch
\* reconfigurations and out-of-order order delivery.
BoundedCapacity == \A l \in Levels : book[l] <= CAP

A stock exchange runs an opening auction that collects orders into an order book
before the cross. Each price level has a hard capacity on how many orders may
rest there. Traders submit orders that travel over an unordered gateway, so
order messages arrive at the matching engine in any order; each order carries the
auction epoch it was submitted under. An order rests in the book only if it is
from the current epoch and its price level still has spare capacity; an order
from a superseded epoch is rejected without touching the book. A resting order
may be cancelled, freeing its slot. Epoch-numbered reconfiguration starts a fresh
auction round: the epoch is bumped and the book is cleared, so any orders still
in flight from the previous round become stale and are rejected on arrival.

---- MODULE W4Od9m7p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Loads == {"g1", "g2"}
Instances == {"A", "B"}

VARIABLES reg, pending, done, demand

vars == <<reg, pending, done, demand>>

MAXD == 3

\* reg[l] is the compare-and-swap register for load l: "armed" (still online) or
\* "shed" (breaker tripped -- an irreversible action). done logs every trip that
\* actually fired, with the shedder instance that fired it.
Init ==
    /\ reg = [l \in Loads |-> "armed"]
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ done = {}
    /\ demand = MAXD

\* When grid demand is high, a shedder instance queues a compare-and-swap trip
\* request against a load it believes is still armed.
Submit(inst, l) ==
    /\ demand > 0
    /\ reg[l] = "armed"
    /\ ~ \E r \in pending : r.inst = inst /\ r.load = l
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {[inst |-> inst, load |-> l]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, done, demand>>

\* CAS succeeds only if the load is still armed; it trips the breaker (armed ->
\* shed), records the responsible instance, and relieves one unit of demand.
ApplyCAS(r) ==
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ reg[r.load] = "armed"
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![r.load] = "shed"]
    /\ done' = done \cup {[load |-> r.load, inst |-> r.inst]}
    /\ demand' = IF demand > 0 THEN demand - 1 ELSE 0
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}

\* CAS fails: another instance already shed this load, so the request is dropped
\* (the trip is not repeated).
FailCAS(r) ==
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ reg[r.load] = "shed"
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, done, demand>>

\* Demand can rise again (load returns), re-motivating shedding of still-armed
\* loads; already-shed breakers stay shed.
DemandRise ==
    /\ demand < MAXD
    /\ demand' = demand + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, pending, done>>

AllShed == \A l \in Loads : reg[l] = "shed"

Idle ==
    /\ AllShed
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E inst \in Instances, l \in Loads : Submit(inst, l)
    \/ \E r \in pending : ApplyCAS(r)
    \/ \E r \in pending : FailCAS(r)
    \/ DemandRise
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [Loads -> {"armed", "shed"}]
    /\ pending \subseteq [inst : Instances, load : Loads]
    /\ done \subseteq [load : Loads, inst : Instances]
    /\ demand \in 0..MAXD

\* An irreversible trip happens at most once per load: even though two independent
\* shedder instances share the load pool, no load is ever recorded as tripped by
\* two different instances (the CAS guard admits a single winner).
ShedAtMostOnce ==
    \A e1 \in done, e2 \in done : (e1.load = e2.load) => (e1.inst = e2.inst)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ShedAtMostOnce
nl:
A power-grid load shedder protects the grid by tripping breakers to drop load
when demand runs high. Two independent shedder instances share one pool of
sheddable loads. Each load has a compare-and-swap register reading either armed
(online) or shed (breaker tripped); tripping a breaker is irreversible. When
demand is high, a shedder instance queues a compare-and-swap trip request against
a load it believes is still armed. The CAS succeeds only if the load is still
armed at apply time, in which case it trips the breaker, records which instance
fired the trip, and relieves one unit of demand; if the load was already shed by
the other instance, the CAS fails and the request is dropped rather than
re-tripping. Demand can rise again, re-motivating shedding of still-armed loads,
but already-shed breakers stay shed. When all loads are shed and no request is
pending, the shedder idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No load's breaker is ever tripped by two different instances, so the irreversible trip happens at most once per load despite the shared pool.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m2p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Drones == {"d1", "d2"}
Votes == {"yes", "no"}
MAXR == 2
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES phase, rnd, votes, inbox

vars == <<phase, rnd, votes, inbox>>

Phases == {"idle", "voting", "committed"}

\* votes[d] is the tallied vote from drone d in the CURRENT round (or NONE):
\* a record carrying the vote and the round it was cast under.
Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ rnd = 1
    /\ votes = [d \in Drones |-> [set |-> FALSE, v |-> "yes", rnd |-> 0]]
    /\ inbox = {}

\* The coordinator opens a two-phase-commit round for a mission action.
Propose ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ votes' = [d \in Drones |-> [set |-> FALSE, v |-> "yes", rnd |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rnd, inbox>>

\* A drone casts its vote, stamping it with the round it believes is current.
CastVote(d, v) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ ~ \E m \in inbox : m.drone = d
    /\ ~ votes[d].set
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[drone |-> d, v |-> v, rnd |-> rnd]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, rnd, votes>>

\* The coordinator tallies a vote ONLY if it is from the current round; a vote
\* from a stale (superseded) round is never counted.
Deliver(m) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.rnd = rnd
    /\ ~ votes[m.drone].set
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![m.drone] = [set |-> TRUE, v |-> m.v, rnd |-> m.rnd]]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, rnd>>

\* A stale-round vote (from a drone that missed a reconfiguration) is discarded,
\* not applied.
DropStale(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.rnd # rnd
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, rnd, votes>>

\* Commit needs a unanimous yes from all drones in the current round.
Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A d \in Drones : votes[d].set /\ votes[d].v = "yes"
    /\ phase' = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rnd, votes, inbox>>

\* Any no vote aborts the round back to idle.
Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \E d \in Drones : votes[d].set /\ votes[d].v = "no"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ votes' = [d \in Drones |-> [set |-> FALSE, v |-> "yes", rnd |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rnd, inbox>>

\* A drone may be slow (still deciding); it never fails, so voting stays open.
Slow(d) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ ~ votes[d].set
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

\* Reconfiguration starts a new round; votes reset but in-flight messages linger
\* and become stale.
NewRound ==
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "committed"}
    /\ rnd < MAXR
    /\ rnd' = rnd + 1
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ votes' = [d \in Drones |-> [set |-> FALSE, v |-> "yes", rnd |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED inbox

Idle ==
    /\ phase = "committed"
    /\ rnd = MAXR
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ Propose
    \/ \E d \in Drones, v \in Votes : CastVote(d, v)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Deliver(m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : DropStale(m)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Slow(d)
    \/ NewRound
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in Phases
    /\ rnd \in 1..MAXR
    /\ votes \in [Drones -> [set : BOOLEAN, v : Votes, rnd : 0..MAXR]]
    /\ inbox \subseteq [drone : Drones, v : Votes, rnd : 1..MAXR]

\* No stale or unauthorized participant's action is ever counted: every vote in
\* the current tally was cast under the current round.
NoStaleAction ==
    \A d \in Drones : votes[d].set => (votes[d].rnd = rnd)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleAction
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm coordinates each mission action through
two-phase commit. A coordinator opens a voting round for an action, and every
drone casts a yes or no vote stamped with the round number it believes is
current. The coordinator counts a vote only if it is from the current round; a
vote stamped with a stale, superseded round (from a drone that missed a
reconfiguration) is discarded rather than counted. The action commits only on a
unanimous yes from the current round; any no vote aborts the round back to idle.
A drone may be slow, still deciding and not yet having voted, but it never fails,
so the round stays open for it. Reconfiguration starts a new round, resetting the
tally while any votes still in flight from the old round linger and become stale.
When the final round has committed, the swarm idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No stale or unauthorized participant's vote is ever counted; every vote in the current tally was cast under the current round.

---- MODULE W4Od15m6p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Symbols == {"s1", "s2"}
Nodes == {"n1", "n2"}
MAXT == 3
LEASE == 2
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES lease, printed, plog, clock, crashed

vars == <<lease, printed, plog, clock, crashed>>

\* lease[s] = [owner, exp]: the node holding the print lease on symbol s and the
\* clock time at which that lease expires. printed[s] marks the (irreversible)
\* opening cross print. plog logs each print with the node that made it.
Init ==
    /\ lease = [s \in Symbols |-> [owner |-> NONE, exp |-> 0]]
    /\ printed = [s \in Symbols |-> FALSE]
    /\ plog = {}
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ crashed = {}

Valid(s) == lease[s].owner # NONE /\ lease[s].exp > clock

\* A live node acquires the lease on an as-yet-unprinted symbol if the symbol's
\* lease is free or has expired; the lease runs LEASE ticks.
Acquire(n, s) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ ~ printed[s]
    /\ ~ Valid(s)
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = [owner |-> n, exp |-> clock + LEASE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<printed, plog, clock, crashed>>

\* Printing is the irreversible cross; it requires a still-valid lease held by the
\* acting node and consumes that lease.
Print(n, s) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ ~ printed[s]
    /\ lease[s].owner = n
    /\ lease[s].exp > clock
    /\ printed' = [printed EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
    /\ plog' = plog \cup {[sym |-> s, node |-> n]}
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = [owner |-> NONE, exp |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, crashed>>

\* Time advances; leases can expire.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < MAXT
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, printed, plog, crashed>>

\* A node can crash silently; its lease is not released and simply expires with
\* time, letting another node take over.
Crash(n) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, printed, plog, clock>>

Idle ==
    /\ (\A s \in Symbols : printed[s]) \/ (crashed = Nodes)
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, s \in Symbols : Acquire(n, s)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, s \in Symbols : Print(n, s)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ lease \in [Symbols -> [owner : Nodes \cup {NONE}, exp : 0..(MAXT + LEASE)]]
    /\ printed \in [Symbols -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ plog \subseteq [sym : Symbols, node : Nodes]
    /\ clock \in 0..MAXT
    /\ crashed \subseteq Nodes

\* The irreversible cross happens at most once per symbol: no symbol is ever
\* printed by two different nodes (lease exclusivity admits a single printer).
PrintAtMostOnce ==
    \A e1 \in plog, e2 \in plog : (e1.sym = e2.sym) => (e1.node = e2.node)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PrintAtMostOnce
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction prints the opening cross for each symbol exactly
once. Matching nodes coordinate through lease-based ownership with expiry: to be
allowed to print a symbol a node must first acquire that symbol's print lease,
which it can take only if the symbol is not yet printed and its lease is free or
has already expired. A lease runs for a fixed number of clock ticks and then
expires. Printing the opening cross is irreversible; it requires the acting node
to still hold a valid, unexpired lease on the symbol, and it consumes that lease.
Time advances tick by tick, expiring stale leases. A node can crash silently at
any time; its lease is not actively released but simply expires with the clock,
letting another node acquire the symbol and print it. When every symbol is
printed, or every node has crashed, the auction idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The opening cross for a symbol is printed at most once, since lease exclusivity means no symbol is ever printed by two different nodes.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m6p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Instances == {"A", "B"}
TOTAL == 3
MAXT == 3
LEASE == 2

VARIABLES avail, loan, clock, leaseEnd

vars == <<avail, loan, clock, leaseEnd>>

\* avail = copies sitting in the shared pool; loan[i] = copies instance i has
\* leased out to patrons; leaseEnd[i] = clock time i's outstanding leases expire.
Init ==
    /\ avail = TOTAL
    /\ loan = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ leaseEnd = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

\* An instance leases one copy out of the shared pool to a patron, setting the
\* expiry of its outstanding leases a fixed horizon ahead.
Lease(i) ==
    /\ avail > 0
    /\ avail' = avail - 1
    /\ loan' = [loan EXCEPT ![i] = @ + 1]
    /\ leaseEnd' = [leaseEnd EXCEPT ![i] = clock + LEASE]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* A patron returns a leased copy early; it goes back to the shared pool.
Return(i) ==
    /\ loan[i] > 0
    /\ loan' = [loan EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1]
    /\ avail' = avail + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, leaseEnd>>

\* A lease that has reached its expiry time is reclaimed: the copy returns to the
\* shared pool automatically.
Expire(i) ==
    /\ loan[i] > 0
    /\ clock >= leaseEnd[i]
    /\ loan' = [loan EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1]
    /\ avail' = avail + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, leaseEnd>>

\* Time advances, allowing leases to expire.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < MAXT
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<avail, loan, leaseEnd>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Lease(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Return(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Expire(i)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ avail \in 0..TOTAL
    /\ loan \in [Instances -> 0..TOTAL]
    /\ clock \in 0..MAXT
    /\ leaseEnd \in [Instances -> 0..(MAXT + LEASE)]

\* No copy is ever created or destroyed: copies in the shared pool plus copies
\* leased out across both instances always sum to the fixed total.
Conservation == avail + loan["A"] + loan["B"] = TOTAL
====

NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conservation

A library book reservation system manages a shared pool of identical copies of a
title. Two independent reservation instances draw from the same pool. Ownership
of a copy is handled by lease-based ownership with expiry: an instance leases one
copy out of the shared pool to a patron and sets an expiry a fixed number of
ticks ahead. A leased copy returns to the shared pool in one of two ways: a
patron returns it early, or its lease reaches its expiry time and is
automatically reclaimed. Time advances tick by tick, which is what lets leases
reach expiry. Because both instances take from and return to the one shared pool,
the total number of physical copies must never change.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of copies sitting in the shared pool plus the copies leased out across both instances always equals the fixed total, so no copy is ever created or destroyed.

---- MODULE W4Od16m8p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Dispensers == {"p1", "p2"}
Drugs == {"dA", "dB"}
CAP == 2
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES coarse, fine, dispensed, pc, crashed

vars == <<coarse, fine, dispensed, pc, crashed>>

\* coarse = holder of the cabinet (coarse) lock. fine[d] = holder of the fine lock
\* on drug slot d. Dispensers must take the coarse lock first, then a fine lock.
Init ==
    /\ coarse = NONE
    /\ fine = [d \in Drugs |-> NONE]
    /\ dispensed = [d \in Drugs |-> 0]
    /\ pc = [p \in Dispensers |-> "idle"]
    /\ crashed = {}

\* Acquire the coarse cabinet lock (first level of the hierarchy).
AcqCoarse(p) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ pc[p] = "idle"
    /\ coarse = NONE
    /\ coarse' = p
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![p] = "coarse"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, dispensed, crashed>>

\* Holding the coarse lock, acquire a fine lock on a specific drug slot.
AcqFine(p, d) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ pc[p] = "coarse"
    /\ coarse = p
    /\ fine[d] = NONE
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![d] = p]
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![p] = "fine"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, dispensed, crashed>>

\* Dispense one unit from a locked slot, only while stock capacity remains.
Dispense(p, d) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ pc[p] = "fine"
    /\ fine[d] = p
    /\ dispensed[d] < CAP
    /\ dispensed' = [dispensed EXCEPT ![d] = @ + 1]
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![p] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, crashed>>

\* Release all locks held by p (used after dispensing, or to back out when the
\* slot is at capacity).
Release(p) ==
    /\ pc[p] \in {"coarse", "fine", "done"}
    /\ coarse' = IF coarse = p THEN NONE ELSE coarse
    /\ fine' = [d \in Drugs |-> IF fine[d] = p THEN NONE ELSE fine[d]]
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispensed, crashed>>

\* A dispenser can crash silently, still holding its locks.
Crash(p) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, dispensed, pc>>

\* Recovery reclaims the locks a crashed dispenser was holding.
Recover(p) ==
    /\ p \in crashed
    /\ pc[p] # "idle"
    /\ coarse' = IF coarse = p THEN NONE ELSE coarse
    /\ fine' = [d \in Drugs |-> IF fine[d] = p THEN NONE ELSE fine[d]]
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispensed, crashed>>

Idle ==
    /\ crashed = Dispensers
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Dispensers : AcqCoarse(p)
    \/ \E p \in Dispensers, d \in Drugs : AcqFine(p, d)
    \/ \E p \in Dispensers, d \in Drugs : Dispense(p, d)
    \/ \E p \in Dispensers : Release(p)
    \/ \E p \in Dispensers : Crash(p)
    \/ \E p \in Dispensers : Recover(p)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Dispensers \cup {NONE}
    /\ fine \in [Drugs -> Dispensers \cup {NONE}]
    /\ dispensed \in [Drugs -> 0..CAP]
    /\ pc \in [Dispensers -> {"idle", "coarse", "fine", "done"}]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Dispensers

\* No drug slot ever dispenses more units than its stocked capacity.
BoundedCapacity == \A d \in Drugs : dispensed[d] <= CAP
====

NEXT Next
INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser serializes access to a medication cabinet with
hierarchical locks. To dispense a drug, a dispensing unit must first take the
coarse cabinet lock, then take a fine lock on the specific drug slot, and only
then dispense a unit from that slot. A slot may be dispensed from only while it
still has stocked capacity remaining. After dispensing, or when it needs to back
out because the slot is at capacity, a unit releases every lock it holds. A
dispensing unit can crash silently while still holding its locks; a recovery step
reclaims the locks a crashed unit was holding so other units can proceed. When
every dispensing unit has crashed, the system idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No drug slot ever dispenses more units than its stocked capacity, even under hierarchical locking, silent crashes, and lock recovery.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m3p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Nodes == {"n1", "n2"}
Patrons == {"pa", "pb"}
Shelves == {"sl1", "sl2", "sl3"}
MAXTERM == 3
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES leader, term, alive, held, active

vars == <<leader, term, alive, held, active>>

\* held[p] = set of shelves currently reserved by patron p. active = the set of
\* shelves provisioned right now (capacity can grow and shrink at runtime).
Init ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ term = 0
    /\ alive = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]
    /\ held = [p \in Patrons |-> {}]
    /\ active = {"sl1"}

LiveLeader == (leader # NONE) /\ alive[leader]
HeldBy(s) == \E p \in Patrons : s \in held[p]

\* A surviving node with no live leader wins a higher term and leads.
Elect(n) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ ~ LiveLeader
    /\ term < MAXTERM
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, held, active>>

\* The leader may crash silently; a survivor fails over into leadership.
Crash ==
    /\ LiveLeader
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![leader] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, held, active>>

\* The leader reserves a currently-provisioned, unreserved shelf for a patron.
Reserve(p, s) ==
    /\ LiveLeader
    /\ s \in active
    /\ ~ HeldBy(s)
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![p] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, alive, active>>

\* A patron gives up a shelf it holds.
Release(p, s) ==
    /\ s \in held[p]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![p] = @ \ {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, alive, active>>

\* Capacity grows: the leader provisions a new shelf into service.
AddShelf(s) ==
    /\ LiveLeader
    /\ s \notin active
    /\ active' = active \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, alive, held>>

\* Capacity shrinks: the leader retires an unreserved shelf from service.
RemoveShelf(s) ==
    /\ LiveLeader
    /\ s \in active
    /\ ~ HeldBy(s)
    /\ active' = active \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, alive, held>>

AllDead == \A n \in Nodes : ~ alive[n]

Idle ==
    /\ AllDead \/ (~ LiveLeader /\ term = MAXTERM)
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ Crash
    \/ \E p \in Patrons, s \in Shelves : Reserve(p, s)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons, s \in Shelves : Release(p, s)
    \/ \E s \in Shelves : AddShelf(s)
    \/ \E s \in Shelves : RemoveShelf(s)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {NONE}
    /\ term \in 0..MAXTERM
    /\ alive \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ held \in [Patrons -> SUBSET Shelves]
    /\ active \subseteq Shelves

\* No shelf is ever double-allocated: no shelf appears in two different patrons'
\* reservation sets at the same time, across leader failover and runtime capacity
\* changes.
NoDoubleAlloc ==
    \A p1 \in Patrons, p2 \in Patrons, s \in Shelves :
        (s \in held[p1] /\ s \in held[p2]) => (p1 = p2)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAlloc
nl:
A library book reservation system runs across a pair of server nodes that fail
over. One node is the elected leader on a monotonically increasing term, and when
there is no live leader a surviving node wins a higher term and takes over. The
leader is the only node that reserves shelves. The set of provisioned shelves
changes at runtime: the leader can grow capacity by provisioning a new shelf into
service, and shrink capacity by retiring an unreserved shelf. The leader reserves
a currently-provisioned, unreserved shelf for a patron; a patron may later
release a shelf it holds. The leader can crash silently, after which a survivor
fails over into leadership on a higher term. When every node has crashed, or no
leader can be elected because the term ceiling is reached, the system idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No shelf is ever reserved by two different patrons at the same time, across leader failover and runtime capacity changes.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od2m8p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Robots == {"r1", "r2"}
Bins == {"b1", "b2"}
MsgIds == {1, 2, 3}
TOTAL == 3
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES coarse, fine, count, transit, pc

vars == <<coarse, fine, count, transit, pc>>

\* Robots share one aisle guarded by a coarse lock and per-bin fine locks. count[b]
\* is the stock in bin b; transit holds in-flight transfer messages (amount 1 each)
\* delivered in any order. Conservation must hold across bins plus transit.
Init ==
    /\ coarse = NONE
    /\ fine = [b \in Bins |-> NONE]
    /\ count = [b \in Bins |-> IF b = "b1" THEN TOTAL ELSE 0]
    /\ transit = {}
    /\ pc = [r \in Robots |-> "idle"]

RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumOver(f, S \ {x})

RECURSIVE SumTransit(_)
SumTransit(T) ==
    IF T = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET m == CHOOSE y \in T : TRUE IN m.amt + SumTransit(T \ {m})

\* Take the coarse aisle lock (first level).
AcqCoarse(r) ==
    /\ pc[r] = "idle"
    /\ coarse = NONE
    /\ coarse' = r
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![r] = "coarse"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, count, transit>>

\* Holding the coarse lock, take the fine lock on the source bin (second level).
AcqFine(r, b) ==
    /\ pc[r] = "coarse"
    /\ coarse = r
    /\ fine[b] = NONE
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = r]
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![r] = "fine"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, count, transit>>

\* Withdraw one unit from the locked source bin, put it in transit toward a
\* destination bin, and release both locks.
Withdraw(r, src, dst, id) ==
    /\ pc[r] = "fine"
    /\ coarse = r
    /\ fine[src] = r
    /\ count[src] > 0
    /\ ~ \E m \in transit : m.id = id
    /\ count' = [count EXCEPT ![src] = @ - 1]
    /\ transit' = transit \cup {[id |-> id, to |-> dst, amt |-> 1]}
    /\ coarse' = NONE
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![src] = NONE]
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]

\* A transfer message is delivered in any order, crediting the destination bin.
Deliver(m) ==
    /\ m \in transit
    /\ count' = [count EXCEPT ![m.to] = @ + m.amt]
    /\ transit' = transit \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, pc>>

\* Back out of held locks without moving anything (e.g., the locked bin is empty).
Abort(r) ==
    /\ pc[r] \in {"coarse", "fine"}
    /\ coarse' = IF coarse = r THEN NONE ELSE coarse
    /\ fine' = [b \in Bins |-> IF fine[b] = r THEN NONE ELSE fine[b]]
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<count, transit>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots : AcqCoarse(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, b \in Bins : AcqFine(r, b)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, src \in Bins, dst \in Bins, id \in MsgIds : Withdraw(r, src, dst, id)
    \/ \E m \in transit : Deliver(m)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Abort(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Robots \cup {NONE}
    /\ fine \in [Bins -> Robots \cup {NONE}]
    /\ count \in [Bins -> 0..TOTAL]
    /\ transit \subseteq [id : MsgIds, to : Bins, amt : {1}]
    /\ pc \in [Robots -> {"idle", "coarse", "fine"}]

\* Nothing is created or destroyed: the stock across all bins plus the units in
\* transit always equals the fixed warehouse total.
Conservation == SumOver(count, Bins) + SumTransit(transit) = TOTAL
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet moves stock between storage bins that all sit in one
aisle. Robots coordinate with hierarchical locks: a robot first takes the coarse
aisle lock, then takes the fine lock on the specific source bin it wants to draw
from. Holding both locks, it withdraws one unit from the locked bin, places the
unit in transit toward a destination bin, and immediately releases both locks.
Transfer messages ride an unordered conveyor-control bus, so they are delivered
in any order, and delivery simply credits the destination bin with the unit. If a
robot finds its locked bin empty it can back out, releasing its held locks
without moving anything. Every unit is either resting in some bin or in transit
between bins.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The stock across all bins plus the units currently in transit always equals the fixed warehouse total, so nothing is ever created or destroyed.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m4p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences

Procs == {"P1", "P2"}
Vals == {"v1", "v2"}
QCAP == 2
MAXVER == 3
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES queue, rec, applied, working

vars == <<queue, rec, applied, working>>

\* queue is a bounded work queue of update ops (backpressure when full). rec is
\* the shared auction record [val, ver]. applied logs committed writes. working[p]
\* is the op processor p is currently handling, with the version it read (exp).
NoOp == [val |-> NONE, exp |-> 0]

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ rec = [val |-> "init", ver |-> 0]
    /\ applied = {[ver |-> 0, val |-> "init"]}
    /\ working = [p \in Procs |-> NoOp]

\* Producers enqueue an update op; backpressure blocks enqueue when the queue is
\* full.
Enqueue(v) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < QCAP
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [val |-> v])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, applied, working>>

\* A free processor takes the head op and snapshots the record's current version.
Take(p) ==
    /\ working[p].val = NONE
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![p] = [val |-> Head(queue).val, exp |-> rec.ver]]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, applied>>

\* Commit succeeds only if the record's version is unchanged since the snapshot
\* (no lost update); it advances the version and logs the write.
Commit(p) ==
    /\ working[p].val # NONE
    /\ working[p].exp = rec.ver
    /\ rec.ver < MAXVER
    /\ rec' = [val |-> working[p].val, ver |-> rec.ver + 1]
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {[ver |-> rec.ver + 1, val |-> working[p].val]}
    /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![p] = NoOp]
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

\* If the record moved under it, the processor re-snapshots and retries its op
\* rather than blindly overwriting (which would lose the intervening update).
Retry(p) ==
    /\ working[p].val # NONE
    /\ working[p].exp # rec.ver
    /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![p].exp = rec.ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, rec, applied>>

\* A processor can be slow: it may hold its op without progressing. It never
\* fails, so it stays able to commit or retry later.
Slow(p) ==
    /\ working[p].val # NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E v \in Vals : Enqueue(v)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Take(p)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Commit(p)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Retry(p)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Slow(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq([val : Vals])
    /\ rec \in [val : Vals \cup {"init"}, ver : 0..MAXVER]
    /\ applied \subseteq [ver : 0..MAXVER, val : Vals \cup {"init"}]
    /\ working \in [Procs -> [val : Vals \cup {NONE}, exp : 0..MAXVER]]

\* No committed update to the shared record is ever silently lost: no applied
\* write claims a version beyond the record's, and the applied write holding the
\* record's current version agrees with the record's current value.
NoLostUpdate ==
    \A a \in applied :
        /\ a.ver <= rec.ver
        /\ (a.ver = rec.ver) => (a.val = rec.val)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction feeds incoming order updates through a bounded
work queue with backpressure into a shared auction record that carries a value
and a version counter. Producers enqueue update ops, but when the queue is full
backpressure blocks further enqueues until space frees up. Two processors drain
the queue concurrently: a free processor takes the head op and snapshots the
record's current version. It commits its update only if the record's version is
unchanged since that snapshot, which advances the version and logs the write; if
the record moved under it, the processor re-snapshots and retries its op rather
than blindly overwriting an update another processor made in between. A processor
can be slow, holding its op without progressing for a while, but it never fails,
so it stays able to commit or retry later.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No committed update to the shared auction record is ever silently overwritten, so the applied write holding the record's current version always agrees with the record's current value.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m1p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets, TLC

Nodes == {"n1", "n2", "n3"}
MsgIds == {1, 2, 3}
CAP == 2
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES tokensAt, transit, pc, served

vars == <<tokensAt, transit, pc, served>>

\* A single ring token grants exclusive dispatch rights. tokensAt[n] in {0,1} is
\* the token count parked at controller n; transit holds the token while it is
\* being handed to the next controller on the ring. The token is never created or
\* destroyed. served[n] counts dispatch actions n performed while holding it.
Ring == ("n1" :> "n2") @@ ("n2" :> "n3") @@ ("n3" :> "n1")

Init ==
    /\ tokensAt = [n \in Nodes |-> IF n = "n1" THEN 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ transit = {}
    /\ pc = [n \in Nodes |-> "idle"]
    /\ served = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]

RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumOver(f, S \ {x})

RECURSIVE SumTransit(_)
SumTransit(T) ==
    IF T = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET m == CHOOSE y \in T : TRUE IN m.amt + SumTransit(T \ {m})

\* The token holder enters its exclusive dispatch section.
EnterCS(n) ==
    /\ tokensAt[n] = 1
    /\ pc[n] = "idle"
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![n] = "cs"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokensAt, transit, served>>

\* While in its section, the holder performs a bounded amount of dispatch work.
Serve(n) ==
    /\ pc[n] = "cs"
    /\ served[n] < CAP
    /\ served' = [served EXCEPT ![n] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokensAt, transit, pc>>

\* The holder passes the single token to the next controller on the ring, putting
\* it in transit and leaving its own section.
Pass(n, id) ==
    /\ tokensAt[n] = 1
    /\ ~ \E m \in transit : m.id = id
    /\ tokensAt' = [tokensAt EXCEPT ![n] = 0]
    /\ transit' = transit \cup {[id |-> id, to |-> Ring[n], amt |-> 1]}
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![n] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED served

\* The next controller receives the token.
Receive(m) ==
    /\ m \in transit
    /\ tokensAt' = [tokensAt EXCEPT ![m.to] = @ + m.amt]
    /\ transit' = transit \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pc, served>>

\* The holder can be slow, keeping the token without acting; it never fails, so
\* it can still serve or pass later.
Slow(n) ==
    /\ tokensAt[n] = 1
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : EnterCS(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Serve(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, id \in MsgIds : Pass(n, id)
    \/ \E m \in transit : Receive(m)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Slow(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ tokensAt \in [Nodes -> 0..1]
    /\ transit \subseteq [id : MsgIds, to : Nodes, amt : {1}]
    /\ pc \in [Nodes -> {"idle", "cs"}]
    /\ served \in [Nodes -> 0..CAP]

\* The token is never created or destroyed: the token count parked across all
\* controllers plus the count in transit on the ring always equals one.
Conservation == SumOver(tokensAt, Nodes) + SumTransit(transit) = 1
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper grants exclusive dispatch rights to its
controllers using a token ring: a single token circulates around the ring, and
only the controller currently holding the token may dispatch cars. The holder
enters its exclusive dispatch section, performs a bounded amount of dispatch work
while holding the token, and then passes the single token to the next controller
on the ring. Passing the token puts it in transit toward the next controller,
which then receives it. A controller can be slow, keeping the token without
acting for a while, but it never fails, so it can still serve or pass the token
later. The token is a single physical grant that is only ever handed along the
ring, never duplicated or dropped.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The token is never created or destroyed: the token count parked across all controllers plus the count in transit on the ring always equals exactly one.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m7p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Workers == {"A1", "A2", "B1"}
CAP == 2
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES lockReg, pc, ledger, pending

vars == <<lockReg, pc, ledger, pending>>

\* lockReg is the compare-and-swap lock register guarding the shared reservation
\* ledger (the critical resource). Workers belong to two independent reservation
\* instances (A*, B*) that share the one ledger. pc[w] tracks each worker.
Init ==
    /\ lockReg = NONE
    /\ pc = [w \in Workers |-> "idle"]
    /\ ledger = 0
    /\ pending = {}

\* A worker submits a compare-and-swap acquire against the lock, expecting it free.
Submit(w) ==
    /\ pc[w] = "idle"
    /\ ~ \E r \in pending : r.worker = w
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {[worker |-> w, exp |-> NONE]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lockReg, pc, ledger>>

\* CAS succeeds only if the register still equals the expected (free) value; the
\* winner takes the lock and enters the critical section.
ApplyCAS(r) ==
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ lockReg = r.exp
    /\ lockReg' = r.worker
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![r.worker] = "cs"]
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED ledger

\* CAS fails: the lock was taken by someone else, so the request is dropped and
\* the worker will retry.
FailCAS(r) ==
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ lockReg # r.exp
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lockReg, pc, ledger>>

\* Inside the critical section a worker mutates the shared ledger (bounded work).
Work(w) ==
    /\ pc[w] = "cs"
    /\ lockReg = w
    /\ ledger < CAP
    /\ ledger' = ledger + 1
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![w] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lockReg, pending>>

\* Releasing frees the lock register (CAS back to free) and returns to idle.
Release(w) ==
    /\ pc[w] \in {"cs", "done"}
    /\ lockReg = w
    /\ lockReg' = NONE
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![w] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, pending>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Submit(w)
    \/ \E r \in pending : ApplyCAS(r)
    \/ \E r \in pending : FailCAS(r)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Work(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Release(w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ lockReg \in Workers \cup {NONE}
    /\ pc \in [Workers -> {"idle", "cs", "done"}]
    /\ ledger \in 0..CAP
    /\ pending \subseteq [worker : Workers, exp : {NONE}]

\* Mutual exclusion of the shared ledger: any worker inside or holding the
\* critical section is the lock register's current owner. Since the register
\* names a single owner, at most one worker is ever in the critical section.
MutualExclusion ==
    \A w \in Workers : (pc[w] \in {"cs", "done"}) => (lockReg = w)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A library book reservation system runs two independent reservation instances
(call their workers A1, A2 and B1) that share one reservation ledger, the
critical resource. Access to the ledger is guarded by a single compare-and-swap
lock register. A worker submits a compare-and-swap acquire against the lock,
expecting it to read free. The CAS succeeds only if the register still reads free
at apply time, in which case that worker wins the lock and enters the critical
section; if the lock was already taken by another worker the CAS fails and the
request is dropped so the worker can retry. Inside the critical section the
worker mutates the shared ledger, doing a bounded amount of work, and then
releases the lock by compare-and-swapping the register back to free. Because both
instances contend for the same lock, only the register's current owner may be
inside.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one worker is ever inside the critical section, because any worker inside or holding it is the lock register's single current owner.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m2p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Locks == {"L1", "L2", "L3"}
Votes == {"yes", "no"}
TOTAL == 3
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES phase, prop, votes, inbox, keys

vars == <<phase, prop, votes, inbox, keys>>

Phases == {"idle", "voting", "committed", "aborted"}

\* keys[l] = number of access credentials parked at lock l (fixed total). A
\* two-phase-commit round atomically moves one credential from prop.from to
\* prop.to. Vote messages ride an unordered mesh and arrive in any order.
Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ prop = [from |-> NONE, to |-> NONE]
    /\ votes = [l \in Locks |-> NONE]
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ keys = [l \in Locks |-> IF l = "L1" THEN TOTAL ELSE 0]

RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumOver(f, S \ {x})

\* The coordinator opens a round to move a credential between two distinct locks.
Propose(x, y) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ x # y
    /\ keys[x] > 0
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ prop' = [from |-> x, to |-> y]
    /\ votes' = [l \in Locks |-> NONE]
    /\ inbox' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED keys

\* A participant lock posts its yes/no vote onto the unordered mesh.
CastVote(l, v) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ l \in {prop.from, prop.to}
    /\ votes[l] = NONE
    /\ ~ \E m \in inbox : m.lock = l
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[lock |-> l, v |-> v]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, prop, votes, keys>>

\* Votes are delivered to the coordinator in any order.
Deliver(m) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ votes[m.lock] = NONE
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![m.lock] = m.v]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, prop, keys>>

BothVoted == votes[prop.from] # NONE /\ votes[prop.to] # NONE

\* Commit atomically moves one credential; total credentials are unchanged.
Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[prop.from] = "yes"
    /\ votes[prop.to] = "yes"
    /\ keys[prop.from] > 0
    /\ keys' = [keys EXCEPT ![prop.from] = @ - 1, ![prop.to] = @ + 1]
    /\ phase' = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prop, votes, inbox>>

\* Abort leaves credentials untouched.
Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ BothVoted
    /\ ~(votes[prop.from] = "yes" /\ votes[prop.to] = "yes" /\ keys[prop.from] > 0)
    /\ phase' = "aborted"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prop, votes, inbox, keys>>

Reset ==
    /\ phase \in {"committed", "aborted"}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ prop' = [from |-> NONE, to |-> NONE]
    /\ votes' = [l \in Locks |-> NONE]
    /\ inbox' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED keys

Next ==
    \/ \E x \in Locks, y \in Locks : Propose(x, y)
    \/ \E l \in Locks, v \in Votes : CastVote(l, v)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Deliver(m)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in Phases
    /\ prop \in [from : Locks \cup {NONE}, to : Locks \cup {NONE}]
    /\ votes \in [Locks -> Votes \cup {NONE}]
    /\ inbox \subseteq [lock : Locks, v : Votes]
    /\ keys \in [Locks -> 0..TOTAL]

\* No access credential is ever created or destroyed: the credentials parked
\* across all locks always sum to the fixed total, even as 2PC moves them under
\* reordered vote delivery.
Conservation == SumOver(keys, Locks) = TOTAL
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network shares a fixed set of access credentials parked
across its locks. To move a credential from one lock to another, the network runs
two-phase commit so the move is atomic: a coordinator opens a round to move one
credential between two distinct locks, and each of the two participant locks
returns a yes or no vote. Votes travel over an unordered mesh radio, so they
accumulate and may be delivered to the coordinator in any order. The move commits
only if both participants voted yes and the source lock still has a credential,
in which case exactly one credential leaves the source and arrives at the
destination; otherwise the round aborts and no credential moves. After a commit
or abort the coordinator resets to idle and can open another round.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No access credential is ever created or destroyed: the credentials across all locks always sum to the fixed total, even under reordered vote delivery.

Dispensers == {"p1", "p2"}
TOTAL == 3
MAXV == 4

VARIABLES stock, dispensed, version, working

vars == <<stock, dispensed, version, working>>

\* stock = units still in the cabinet; dispensed = units handed out. Their sum is
\* the fixed pill total. version guards the shared inventory record. working[d]
\* records whether dispenser d is mid-transaction and the version it read.
NoTxn == [active |-> FALSE, snap |-> 0]

Init ==
    /\ stock = TOTAL
    /\ dispensed = 0
    /\ version = 0
    /\ working = [d \in Dispensers |-> NoTxn]

\* A dispenser optimistically reads the inventory version to begin a dispense.
Begin(d) ==
    /\ ~ working[d].active
    /\ stock > 0
    /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![d] = [active |-> TRUE, snap |-> version]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, dispensed, version>>

\* Commit succeeds only if the version is unchanged since the read; it moves one
\* unit from stock to dispensed and bumps the version.
Commit(d) ==
    /\ working[d].active
    /\ working[d].snap = version
    /\ stock > 0
    /\ version < MAXV
    /\ stock' = stock - 1
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![d] = NoTxn]

\* If the inventory record moved under it, the dispenser re-reads and retries
\* rather than applying a stale write.
Retry(d) ==
    /\ working[d].active
    /\ working[d].snap # version
    /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![d].snap = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, dispensed, version>>

\* A returned unit is put back, moving one unit from dispensed to stock and
\* bumping the version.
Return ==
    /\ dispensed > 0
    /\ version < MAXV
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed - 1
    /\ stock' = stock + 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED working

\* A dispenser can be slow, holding its open transaction without progressing; it
\* never fails, so it can still commit or retry later.
Slow(d) ==
    /\ working[d].active
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Idle ==
    /\ version = MAXV
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ Idle
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers : Begin(d)
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers : Commit(d)
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers : Retry(d)
    \/ Return
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers : Slow(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ stock \in 0..TOTAL
    /\ dispensed \in 0..TOTAL
    /\ version \in 0..MAXV
    /\ working \in [Dispensers -> [active : BOOLEAN, snap : 0..MAXV]]

\* No pill is ever created or destroyed: units in the cabinet plus units
\* dispensed always sum to the fixed total, despite optimistic retries.
Conservation == stock + dispensed = TOTAL
====

INVARIANT Conservation

A pharmacy prescription dispenser tracks a shared inventory record for a drug,
guarded by a version counter. Every pill is either still in the cabinet or has
been dispensed, and the two counts together are the fixed pill total. Dispensers
use optimistic locking with retry: a dispenser reads the current inventory
version to begin a dispense, then commits only if the version is unchanged since
that read, which moves one unit from stock to dispensed and bumps the version. If
the record moved under it (another dispenser committed first), the dispenser
re-reads and retries rather than applying a stale write. A returned unit is put
back, moving one unit from dispensed to stock and bumping the version. A
dispenser can be slow, holding its open transaction without progressing, but it
never fails, so it can still commit or retry later. When the version ceiling is
reached the system idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No pill is ever created or destroyed: units in the cabinet plus units dispensed always sum to the fixed total, despite optimistic retries.

---- MODULE W4Od6m2p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Controllers == {"f1", "f2", "f3"}
Votes == {"yes", "no"}
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES phase, authorized, tally, inbox

vars == <<phase, authorized, tally, inbox>>

Phases == {"idle", "voting", "committed", "aborted"}

\* authorized = the set of floor controllers currently commissioned to vote (it is
\* reconfigured between rounds). tally[c] is c's counted vote in this round; only
\* authorized controllers' votes are ever counted. inbox is the unordered set of
\* posted votes awaiting the coordinator.
Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ authorized = {"f1", "f2"}
    /\ tally = [c \in Controllers |-> NONE]
    /\ inbox = {}

\* The coordinator opens a two-phase-commit dispatch round.
Propose ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ tally' = [c \in Controllers |-> NONE]
    /\ inbox' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED authorized

\* Any controller (authorized or not) may post a vote onto the bus.
CastVote(c, v) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ ~ \E m \in inbox : m.ctrl = c
    /\ tally[c] = NONE
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[ctrl |-> c, v |-> v]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, authorized, tally>>

\* The coordinator counts a vote ONLY from an authorized controller.
Deliver(m) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.ctrl \in authorized
    /\ tally[m.ctrl] = NONE
    /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![m.ctrl] = m.v]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, authorized>>

\* A vote from an unauthorized (decommissioned or stale) controller is discarded.
DropUnauth(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.ctrl \notin authorized
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, authorized, tally>>

\* Commit requires a unanimous yes from all currently authorized controllers.
Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A c \in authorized : tally[c] = "yes"
    /\ phase' = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, tally, inbox>>

\* Abort once all authorized controllers have voted and it is not a unanimous yes.
Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A c \in authorized : tally[c] # NONE
    /\ \E c \in authorized : tally[c] = "no"
    /\ phase' = "aborted"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, tally, inbox>>

\* An authorized controller can be slow, not yet having voted; it never fails.
Slow(c) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ c \in authorized
    /\ tally[c] = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

\* Between rounds the commission is reconfigured to a new nonempty authorized set.
Reconfig(S) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ S # {}
    /\ authorized' = S
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, tally, inbox>>

Reset ==
    /\ phase \in {"committed", "aborted"}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ tally' = [c \in Controllers |-> NONE]
    /\ inbox' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED authorized

Next ==
    \/ Propose
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, v \in Votes : CastVote(c, v)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Deliver(m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : DropUnauth(m)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Slow(c)
    \/ \E S \in SUBSET Controllers : Reconfig(S)
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in Phases
    /\ authorized \subseteq Controllers
    /\ tally \in [Controllers -> Votes \cup {NONE}]
    /\ inbox \subseteq [ctrl : Controllers, v : Votes]

\* No unauthorized or stale participant's action is ever counted: every counted
\* vote belongs to a currently authorized controller.
NoUnauthorizedAction ==
    \A c \in Controllers : (tally[c] # NONE) => (c \in authorized)
====

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoUnauthorizedAction
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper decides each dispatch through two-phase commit
among its floor controllers. Only controllers currently commissioned (the
authorized set) are entitled to vote; the commission is reconfigured between
rounds, so a decommissioned or stale controller can still try to vote but is no
longer entitled to. The coordinator opens a dispatch round, and any controller
may post a yes or no vote onto the bus, but the coordinator counts a vote only if
it comes from a currently authorized controller; a vote from an unauthorized or
stale controller is discarded rather than counted. The round commits on a
unanimous yes from all authorized controllers, and aborts once they have all
voted and it is not unanimous. An authorized controller can be slow, not yet
having voted, but it never fails, so the round stays open for it. Between rounds
the commission is reconfigured to a new nonempty authorized set.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No unauthorized or stale controller's vote is ever counted; every counted vote belongs to a currently authorized controller.
